newsitem.title: USA: Texaco to make statement on downstream merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Texaco to make statement on downstream merger talk.

text.p: Texaco Inc said it will issue a statement at around 0900 EDT/1300 GMT on a report that it is in talks with Shell Oil Co. and state-owned Saudi Aramco over a three-way merger of their downstream businesses in the United States.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday that Texaco, Shell and Star Enterprise, a joint venture linking the downstream operations of Texaco and Aramco in the eastern U.S., were in talks over a possible downstream merger.
"We will certainly have something to say," said a Texaco spokesman.

An official at Shell, the U.S. unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group said she was not sure whether or not the company would be commenting on the report. Aramco officials weren't immediately available for comment.

The newspaper report said the companies were planning to form two companies, one joining Star and Shell assets in the eastern U.S. and another merging Shell and Texaco's operations, mainly in the west.

Such a merger would be the first large-scale downstream consolidation in the U.S. and would follow a move earlier this year in Europe by British Petroleum and Mobil Corp to joint their downstream operations there.
-- Tony McAuley, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620
